titulo: Degrees of freedom, joints, and limits
lead: "23 to 43 degrees of freedom" is marketing; the joint tree in the file is the body your controller will command. In this lesson you list the G1's 29 joints with limits in degrees and maximum torque, understand why the leg has six, and check that the number matches the actuators.
objetivo: list the G1's joints with limits in degrees and maximum torque, and check that the number of articulated joints matches nu.

aprende.t: The body tree: pelvis, legs, waist, and arms
Why the leg has 6 joints and in what order
Limits are in radians in the file, in degrees in your head
Degrees of freedom in the file × on the manufacturer's spec sheet

hero_alt: Leg of an industrial humanoid robot on a workbench, with the hip, knee, and ankle exposed and a metal protractor beside it.

secoes.titulo: The 29 joints of the G1 from Menagerie
secoes.sub: Each block is a branch of the tree that starts at the pelvis. Click to see the joints.

nos.detalhe: The root of the tree. It has no motor: the robot only changes place by pushing against the ground. That is why walking is hard.

Six joints per leg, the same count Unitree publishes for the G1. Three in the hip (forward, sideways, and turning), one in the knee, and two in the ankle. With six, the foot can reach any position and orientation within range.
The Menagerie model has 3 joints in the waist. The Unitree spec sheet says 1 in the waist plus 2 optional: this is a difference between versions, not an error.

Seven per arm in the model; Unitree's spec sheet says 5 on the base version's arm. At the wrist, pitch and yaw handle only 5 N·m (the roll, 25): they are for orienting the hand, not for carrying weight.

secoes.legenda: 12 in the legs + 3 in the waist + 14 in the arms = 29 = nu.

secoes.titulo: How to read a line of the tree

texto: left_hip_roll_joint: left leg, hip, roll rotation (tilting sideways). Pitch bends forward and backward; yaw turns around the vertical axis.
The indentation in the output shows what hangs from what: the ankle depends on the knee, which depends on the hip.
The file stores range="-0.087267 2.8798" in radians; the script converts it: -5° to 165° at the knee.
The hip roll is asymmetric and mirrored: left from -30° to 170°, right from -170° to 30°. The leg opens far outward and only a little inward, where the other leg is.
The joint's actuatorfrcrange attribute caps what the motor can do: 139 N·m at the knee, 88 at the hip pitch, 50 at the ankle, 25 at the shoulder, 5 at the wrist pitch and yaw.
This is the model's limit. Resellers quote 90 N·m (base) and 120 N·m (EDU) for the real G1's knee (reported): one more point where the file and the robot can differ.
The total number of joints (njnt=30) includes the free base. The number that matters to the controller is the number of articulated joints, which must match the number of actuators.
If they don't match, there is a passive joint (with no motor) or a motor outside a joint: both change your controller.

abas.rot: Common mistake: counting the base as a degree of freedom
abas.html: abrir.py from lesson 2 prints juntas: 30 (1 base flutuante + 29 articuladas). If you use njnt=30 as the number of motors, you build a command vector with 30 slots and MuJoCo rejects it: ctrl has nu=29. Count only the articulated joints.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after you answer.

perguntas.p: The Menagerie G1 has njnt=30 and nu=29. Where does the difference come from?
opcoes: A neck joint with no motor.
A file error, fixed in newer versions.
The floating base, which is a joint with no motor.
The IMU sensor, which counts as a joint.
perguntas.explica: The free base is a joint (of type free) and has no motor. The 29 articulated joints have one actuator each.

perguntas.p: Why does a humanoid's leg usually have 6 joints?
opcoes: To put the foot in any position and orientation within reach.
Because manufacturers' motors come in packs of six.
Because with fewer than six, the robot can't stand still.
To copy the human leg, which has exactly six identical joints.
perguntas.explica: Position (3) and orientation (3) of the foot call for six degrees of freedom. Three at the hip, one at the knee, and two at the ankle is the G1's arrangement and that of many others.

perguntas.p: Unitree's spec sheet says 1 waist joint; the Menagerie model has 3. How do you handle that?
opcoes: The Menagerie is wrong; use the 1-joint value from the official spec sheet.
Unitree's spec sheet is wrong; use the 3 joints from the file.
Add the two sources together: the robot has 4 waist joints.
They are different versions of the G1; note which version the model represents.
perguntas.explica: The G1 has variants from 23 to 43 degrees of freedom. The model represents one of them; your controller has to match the version of the robot you'll use.

itens.texto: Free pelvis, 6 per leg, 3 at the waist, 7 per arm on the Menagerie G1.
Range in radians and torque in actuatorfrcrange, read from the file.
Articulated joints = nu; the base doesn't count.
